correctness.rationale: The algebra automorphism argument gives (r1,r2)=(6,3) for nonzero linear part. For quadratic-leading f, degree-filtered multiplication gives r1=2+rank[[b,a],[c,b]], and f²=(b²-ac)x²y² gives r2=1 exactly for nonzero discriminant. Cubic-leading and socle cases have ranks (2,0) and (1,0). The nilpotency bound f³=0 reconstructs precisely all six Jordan partitions. The discriminant cone b²=ac has q² points over F_q and a smooth puncture; all other strata are affine opens/products, yielding irreducibility, dimensions and counts. The normalized unit group is exponent3 and generator squaring preserves rank, so subgroup counts equal half element counts. An independent original multiplication-table checker exhaustively verified all 6561 elements over F3 and tested 4716 configurations over F9.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The present theorem specializes to the regular module but enlarges the parameter domain from flat p-point embeddings to *every* element f∈J and every cyclic order-three subgroup of the normalized unit group. It is not a consequence of established constant Jordan type on p-points: the non-flat subgroups cannot satisfy the required independent-linear-part hypotheses. Broader general Jordan theory supplies Jordan rank principles but no located exact full-stratum census.

originality.rationale: The known p-point case is excluded from the new contribution. Relevant primary work defines shifted cyclic subgroup embeddings using nonzero classes in J/J²; the present theorem classifies four distinct J² behavior types and their geometric and arithmetic multiplicities, and no inspected stronger theorem states or implies those claims. Extensive published-finding corpus and primary-literature searches found no exact or dominating published formula. Priority remains provisional because search and source access are not logically exhaustive.
residual_risks: A more general or unindexed Jordan-type classification for complete intersections or modular group algebras could imply the six strata; current open literature comparisons did not locate one.
Not every archival source on modular regular modules was inspected cover-to-cover; a systematic expert historical review remains outstanding.
Geometric strata statements concern reduced locally closed varieties, not scheme-theoretic multiplicities.

value.rationale: All order-three subgroups of the normalized unit group of k[C3×C3] form a natural class of subgroups well beyond the flat π-point restrictions central to established modular representation theory. Classifying their regular-module Jordan types and exact multiplicities over every characteristic-three finite field reveals a nontrivial conic discriminant split and a complete stratification of the 8-dimensional augmentation radical. This is a natural complete classification with arithmetic and geometric content rather than an arbitrary finite sample or a known-table recalculation.
